_about: What each harness of kiln plan 01a1cd8e862e7169a074db3d5fa33f3d (steps 19-28) does through kiln's UI and API, on the host and in a microVM of its own, and each gap with its cited reason (step 35: 'each harness works as on the host, or its gap is listed with a cited reason'). Flags: linux_build (kiln ships an Agentfile pinning its Linux build, for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 alike, so its microVM has a build for every host OS's guest: macOS arm64 (HVF), Linux x86_64 (KVM) and Windows x86_64 (WHP), each guest of its host's architecture); mcp (kiln gives it kiln's MCP server on the host, so an MCP round trip and an agent started from where it runs apply there; what a Windows host gives is a caveat); mcp_in_microvm (kiln gives it kiln's MCP server in a microVM, over the agent-control link's mcp lane, Shards D254, which plan 01a1d2c16eb074f19cf7ae7f1025c0be step 3 names: the drive reads its MCP round trip from inside and the session's link report naming that lane; null: not recorded yet, so the drive tries it); resume (kiln takes its conversation up again: spec.resume, agents_start's resume, an ended agent's Restart); ui_pick_up (the composer's past sessions list its conversations, to pick one up after its agent was ended); link_report (kiln reports the agent-control link of a session in a microVM, runs.control: each end's negotiated suite and group, and its lanes, which the drive's link checks read; a REST drive reads them after every other check whatever this says, and, where kiln's word on the session shows the gap, fails them by its name, vm_e2e::LinkGap, so a run's red says the gap, and once it's gone the links pass or fail on their own). Every flag that is false or null has a gap naming it ({what, where, why, cites}); a gap holds where its where says (the host, a microVM, or both), a microVM's on HVF, KVM and WHP alike unless it names one, and every flag that holds in a microVM is expected to pass on each of them once Hex reports the link (link_report's gap); each caveat is {note, cites}; sources back the row's reason, its pin first. A cite is a URL; kiln's code by the text it holds (path#text: its lines move); or a recorded evidence file's line (docs/research/...:line). Held to kiln's code and to its sources by vm_e2e/step35.rs's checks.

gaps.where: a microVM, on every host OS: macOS arm64 (HVF), Linux x86_64 (KVM) and Windows x86_64 (WHP)
gaps.why: Hex reports no agent-control link: Hex has no Runtime call for it yet. kiln's runner holds its microVMs through Hex's image runtime, whose Runtime (Hex 1969a423e, as kiln vendors it) signals the member and takes kiln's MCP lane over that link but reports nothing of it, so kiln's HexRun::link answers none and the session's runs.control is absent. Expected to pass once Hex has that call (both ends' suite and group, and the link's lanes by Shards' names, mcp:<member> among them) and kiln, vendoring it, maps HexRun::link to it: TLS13_AES_256_GCM_SHA384 at both ends of the agent-control link, and the mcp:<member> lane kiln's MCP from inside rides. Until then a REST drive checks its links after every other check and fails them by this name (vm_e2e::LinkGap).
cites: crates/kiln/src/sandbox/hexvm.rs#Its stdio ride the member's streams from its run host, no link of Shards' agent control.

caveats.note: On a Windows machine kiln gives it its MCP server as a process there only where that machine's kiln is the server (the server's own, by the agent's own token): a runner's own is reached over a Unix socket alone. In a microVM on Windows (WHP) it reaches kiln's MCP over the lane, as on every host OS.
cites: crates/kiln/src/harness/kinds.rs#Without Unix sockets there is no runner of the machine to talk to.

caveats.note: agy's headless stream-json mode can't be asked anything once started: a tool that needs approval is denied, and a stop ends its process, which kiln starts again on the same conversation (--conversation); a message steered in waits for the turn's end. All as on the host.

agy reads MCP servers only from its own mcp_config.json, in the person's volume and so the same for every session: kiln's launch writes its one entry there, the lane's bridge, naming no session, token or address, and the lane names the session, by the member whose connection it hands the runner. Each session's agy is the one member of a microVM of its own, one lane each, and the runner answers each run's connections as that session; two sessions' agy in one member would not be told apart. Two sessions of one person are held so without a VM, over a stand-in lane (owed: ROOT's run of two isolated Antigravity sessions of one person in real microVMs).
